Warning....Don't go - Amazingly rude and very unprofessional
Dec 2025 • Couples
As a visitor to Hanoi we read the reviews.
We decided to go to Viet Restaurant and as the booking was for a very buy night - New Years Eve, we booked well in advance to dine at 9pm. We received an email weeks later (and only a couple of days before NYE) from the restaurant to tell us that as it was NYE we would need to vacate the dining room by 9pm to allow for a reset for a NYE party. We responded and rebooked for 8pm.

I also phoned Viet to confirm this and was told "yes, all good but be aware that you will need to be out by 9pm. "ok" i said"

On NYE we arrived before 8pm to be met in the foyer by the manager who asked "can i help you". Yes please, I responded - "where is the elevator to get to the 8th fl dining room. "don't bother" he said as " the dining room is closing". Yes, I replied we have a booking for 8pm and will vacate by 9. He said "go up if you want".

We went up to the dining room which was full of diners, bar 1 vacant and set table for 2. A waiter came up and said "we are closed". I said" but i have a booking.....!"
He said that kitchen is closed. Another diner came up and said that he had a booking for 7.30pm and said that he was told the same rubbish and that he made sucha fuss that they agreed to serve him if he could order and eat and leave within 30 minutes !

We could see that we were getting nowhere, went downstairs to speak to the hotel manager but he was not interested. 

A happy ending though. we went out and found a lovely table at the nearby restaurant - "The Hanoi Cafe" at 2D P.Yen Thai - it was very nice, great food, lovely sevice and half the price.

Faithful and delicious cuisine in a cozy setting
May 2025 • Couples
We were pleasantly surprised by the quality of the dishes, perfectly faithful to what is presented on the menu. Each bite was a treat, with authentic and well-controlled flavors. The restaurant is located inside the hotel, but the atmosphere is cozy and very pleasant, ideal for a quiet meal.
